hints: Focus on what highest oxidation state means for Period 3 elements from sodium to phosphorus, it is simply the Group number.
Write the highest chloride for each element first, remembering chlorine is -1, so you get NaCl, MgCl2, AlCl3, SiCl4 and PCl5.
Now do the same for the highest oxides with oxygen at -2, work out q divided by p for each, and compare how both ratios change across the period.
walkthrough:
**Find the highest oxidation state**

For Na to P, all outer electrons can be removed or shared. So highest oxidation state = Group number.

$$\text{Na (+I), Mg (+II), Al (+III), Si (+IV), P (+V)}$$

**Work out the highest chlorides**

Chlorine is $\text{Cl}^{-}$, so balance the positive charge of X with enough $\text{Cl}$ atoms.

$$\text{NaCl, MgCl}_{2}, \text{AlCl}_{3}, \text{SiCl}_{4}, \text{PCl}_{5}$$

**Calculate z:y for reaction 1**

Here $z:y$ is number of Cl atoms per X atom.

$$1, 2, 3, 4, 5$$
This is a steady increase from sodium to phosphorus.

**Work out the highest oxides and q:p**

Oxygen is $\text{O}^{2-}$, so balance to give neutral oxides.

$$\text{Na}_{2}\text{O, MgO, Al}_{2}\text{O}_{3}, \text{SiO}_{2}, \text{P}_{2}\text{O}_{5}$$
Now $q:p$ is O atoms per X atom:
$$0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5$$
This also shows a steady increase.

**Conclude**

Since both $z:y$ and $q:p$ increase steadily, the answer is both ratios.

options.A: This is incorrect because both ratios do increase. If you write out the correct highest chlorides and oxides, you see a clear 1,2,3,4,5 pattern for chlorides and 0.5,1,1.5,2,2.5 for oxides.
options.B: This is only half right. z:y does increase steadily (NaCl to PCl5), but q:p also increases steadily, so choosing only z:y misses the oxide trend.
options.C: This is only half right. q:p does increase steadily (Na2O to P2O5), but z:y also increases steadily, so choosing only q:p misses the chloride trend.
options.D: This is correct. Highest chlorides give z:y = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and highest oxides give q:p = 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5. Both show a steady increase from sodium to phosphorus.
